Fix accessory device not connected after AOA mode switch

After connectAndSwitch() sends AOA descriptors, the phone detaches and
re-enumerates as a Google AOA device (18D1:2D00). Previously, onUsbAttach
delegated to checkAlreadyConnectedUsb() which was blocked by the
isConnecting flag still set from the AOA switch phase. Nobody ever
initiated the actual AAP connection to the re-enumerated device.

Fix by making onUsbAttach detect accessory-mode devices and connect
directly via handleConnectionIntent, bypassing checkAlreadyConnectedUsb.
Also reset isConnecting after successful connectAndSwitch in both the
single-USB and last-session paths, since the AOA switch phase is done
and the actual connection will be handled by onUsbAttach.

Additionally fix duplicate stability timer starts when both onCreate
and ACTION_CHECK_USB call checkAlreadyConnectedUsb within milliseconds.

Fix USB auto-connect failing when no permission is granted

The auto-connect flow silently gave up when the app lacked USB host
permission, logging "device found but no permission" without ever
calling UsbManager.requestPermission(). This made USB auto-connect
non-functional on devices where permission wasn't pre-granted via
the system dialog.

Three fixes:

1. Add requestUsbPermission() helper that creates a PendingIntent
   targeting UsbReceiver.ACTION_USB_DEVICE_PERMISSION and calls
   UsbManager.requestPermission(). Called from both
   performSingleUsbConnect() and checkAlreadyConnectedUsb() when
   hasPermission() returns false.

2. Implement the empty onUsbPermission() stub in AapService to
   handle the permission result: on grant, either connect directly
   (accessory mode) or switch to AOA mode (normal device). On deny,
   log a warning.

3. Add resolveUsbDevice() fallback in UsbAttachedActivity for head
   units (e.g. Xtrons Android 10) that send USB_DEVICE_ATTACHED
   intents without the UsbDevice extra. Falls back to
   UsbManager.deviceList when exactly one device is connected.

Fix FLAG_MUTABLE API level check in requestUsbPermission

PendingIntent.FLAG_MUTABLE was introduced in API 31 (S), not API 23
(M). The check used >= M which is incorrect — on API 23-30 the flag
value is inlined at compile time so it won't crash, but the check
should use >= S for correctness.

Introduces CommManager as the single source of truth for connection
lifecycle, replacing scattered broadcast intents with a StateFlow-based
state machine (Disconnected, Connecting, Connected, TransportStarted,

Key changes:
- CommManager centralizes connect/disconnect/handshake logic with

- SSL session resumption via persistent AapSslContext for faster

  activity startup, startReading() begins after video surface is ready
- Enhanced logging with granular LogLevel (replaces boolean debugMode)

  separate state/IO locks in UsbAccessoryConnection

Improve CommManager performance and fix stale accessory reconnection

Performance improvements to CommManager:
- Simplify send() methods: remove unnecessary _scope.launch wrappers
  and dead catch blocks. AapTransport.send() is already thread-safe
  (posts to HandlerThread), so the coroutine overhead was unnecessary
  on every touch/key/sensor event.

- Replace fragile drop(1) with hasEverConnected flag to skip initial

Stale accessory reconnection fix:
- Add onHandshakeFailed() that detects handshake failures on
  accessory-mode devices (stale wireless AA dongles). After 1
  consecutive failure, forces AOA re-enumeration to clear stale
  USB buffers.
- Add USB reconnect scheduling in scheduleReconnectIfNeeded() after
  unexpected USB disconnects.
- Reset accessoryHandshakeFailures counter on successful transport
  start.

Fix USB session crash when resetInterface fails to re-claim

When claimInterface() returned false during a USB interface soft-reset,
the session continued in a broken state — subsequent reads would fail
indefinitely, and the poll loop would spin without ever quitting. This
caused the projection to freeze and eventually crash.

Changes:
- Call disconnect() when claimInterface fails in resetInterface(), so
  the transport detects the dead connection and quits cleanly.
- Check connection.isConnected in AapReadMultipleMessages after a read
  error to propagate the fatal disconnect to the transport loop.
- Increase maxConsecutiveErrorsBeforeReset from 3 to 10 to reduce
  unnecessary interface resets during expected USB silence (channel
  setup, phone UI transitions).

Fix persistent log capture dying silently on MediaTek headunits

The logcat process spawned by startCapture was being killed by the
system after the initial ring buffer dump, causing copyTo() to return
normally with no error. Added automatic restart with watchdog (up to
5 retries with 2s backoff) and append-mode file writing so restarts
preserve previously captured data.

Replace resetInterface() with patience-based USB read error recovery

resetInterface() releases and re-claims the USB interface after 10
consecutive read errors. For direct USB this can recover a stalled
interface, but for wireless dongles (Phone → WiFi → Dongle → USB)
it kills the session entirely, causing USB_DEVICE_DETACHED.

Replace with a tolerance window that gives the dongle up to 60
seconds to recover its WiFi connection from the phone:
- 200ms backoff after 5+ consecutive errors to avoid busy-looping
- Log warnings every 10 errors with duration
- Disconnect cleanly only after 60s of continuous errors
- Log recovery when reads resume

Android's power manager from killing WiFi sockets on charger state
changes. Also passes foregroundServiceType explicitly on Android Q+
to ensure the service gets CONNECTED_DEVICE + MEDIA_PLAYBACK priority.

Shorten reconnecting overlay and add WiFi disconnect dialog

Simplify the reconnecting overlay to just "Connection lost / Retrying…"
for driver safety (less reading while driving). Add a detailed WiFi
disconnect dialog on HomeFragment that advises users to disable
"Switch between networks" or "Network acceleration" in their phone's
WiFi settings, which can aggressively kill WiFi connections without
internet access. Includes translations for all 13 locales.

Fix reconnecting overlay text size and WiFi disconnect dialog trigger

Increase "Connection lost" overlay text from 18sp to 27sp (50% bigger)
for better readability while driving. Fix WiFi disconnect dialog not
showing by removing the lastConnectionType==WIFI condition — wireless
AA dongles connect via USB so the type is "usb", not "wifi". The dialog
message already says "If you were connected wirelessly..." so it
self-filters for the user.

Replace WiFi disconnect dialog with a long Toast

The MaterialAlertDialog was not visible after disconnection (lifecycle
timing issue). Replace with a system-level Toast that shows for ~7s
(two consecutive LENGTH_LONG toasts) so the driver can read the advice
about disabling "Switch between networks" in phone WiFi settings.
Toasts are visible across all activities and screens.

Move WiFi disconnect toast to AapProjectionActivity

Show the toast from AapProjectionActivity on non-clean disconnect
instead of HomeFragment. This ensures it only triggers when projection
was active and the connection was lost (not on every disconnect).
Toasts are system-level so they survive the activity transition back
to HomeFragment. Also fix es-rES translation: teléfono → móvil.

Fix USB reconnect race condition and stale dongle data on reconnect

- Guard accessory-mode connect coroutine with isSwitchingToAccessory flag
  to prevent duplicate concurrent connectUsbWithRetry calls when both
  scheduleReconnectIfNeeded and HomeFragment fire simultaneously

- Skip USB auto-reconnect after VIDEO_FOCUS_NATIVE (user tapped Exit in AA)
  to avoid reconnecting to a stale dongle that still has old TLS data buffered.
  The next USB attach event will trigger a clean connection instead.

- Drain stale data from USB pipe before sending version request during handshake
  so old TLS records from a previous session don't burn the response timeout

Single-USB auto-connect: filter by allowed devices when available

When the user has marked specific devices as "Allowed" in the USB list,
single-USB auto-connect now only counts those devices as candidates.
Non-AA peripherals like dashcams no longer prevent auto-connect.
Falls back to counting all devices on fresh installs (no allowed devices set).

3. Full-screen intent notification (stock Android 10-13, Samsung)
4. Tap-to-open notification as last resort

Add FYT, GLSX, and Microntek ACC/wake intents for head unit auto-start

Extend BootCompleteReceiver to handle ACC ignition and sleep-wake
broadcasts from the most common Chinese head unit platforms:

- FYT (Joying, KLD, FunRover, Witson): ACCON + SLEEP_OUT
- GLSX (FYT variant firmware): ACCON
- Microntek/MTCD/PX3 (cayboy/carboy): ACC_ON

These head units use fast boot and don't send BOOT_COMPLETED on
wake from ACC-off sleep. Without these intents, auto-start on boot
silently fails on most Chinese Android head units.

Add hibernate warning to close-on-disconnect dialog

Explain that some head units hibernate instead of shutting down,
similar to a phone locking its screen, which may prevent the app
from reopening automatically after the first disconnection.

Warn about auto-start on boot conflict with close-on-disconnect

Show a warning when enabling close-on-disconnect while auto-start on
boot is active, explaining that hibernating head units may not trigger
a boot event to reopen the app. The warning is informational only and
does not disable the auto-start setting.

Start service on ACC wake when USB auto-start is enabled

On hibernating head units, USB_DEVICE_ATTACHED may not fire after
wake. When BootCompleteReceiver gets an ACC/wake intent and USB
auto-start is enabled (even without start-on-boot), start AapService
with ACTION_CHECK_USB so it can detect already-connected devices and
register its UsbReceiver for future connections.
implement mediasession transport control

Add hibernate wake detection via SCREEN_ON for Quick Boot head units

On Chinese head units with Quick Boot (hibernate/resume), none of the
known boot or ACC intents fire after waking. This leaves auto-start
completely broken because BootCompleteReceiver never receives anything.

Add a dynamic BroadcastReceiver in AapService that:
- Tracks SCREEN_OFF/SCREEN_ON timing to detect hibernate wakes
  (screen off > 60s = hibernate, not a normal screen timeout)
- Logs all received wake/boot/power/ACC events with "WakeDetect:" prefix
  for diagnostic purposes — users can export logs to help identify what
  broadcasts their specific head unit sends (or doesn't send)
- Triggers auto-start on hibernate wake: launches UI if autoStartOnBoot
  is enabled, checks USB devices if autoStartOnUsb is enabled
- Also listens for POWER_CONNECTED as a secondary wake indicator

ACTION_SCREEN_ON can only be received by dynamically registered receivers
(not manifest-declared), which is why the manifest BootCompleteReceiver
can't catch it — the service must be alive. To ensure this:
- Exit button now keeps the service running in standby when autoStartOnBoot
  is enabled (same pattern as reopenOnReconnection for USB)
- The service survives hibernate (process state preserved in RAM) and its
  dynamic receiver catches SCREEN_ON immediately on wake

Addresses #292 — specifically the case where MediaTek IPO intents also
don't fire on certain firmware versions.

Add "Start on screen on" setting for always-on head units

New auto-start option that triggers on every SCREEN_ON event, designed
for head units that never fully power off (quick boot / hibernate) where
neither BOOT_COMPLETED, MediaTek IPO, nor any OEM ACC intents fire.

When enabled:
- Every SCREEN_ON triggers auto-start (no duration threshold)
- If projection was active: returns directly to AapProjectionActivity
- If not connected: launches MainActivity for auto-connect + checks USB
- Service stays alive on exit to survive hibernate and catch SCREEN_ON

The setting description makes clear this is for head units only, not
phones or tablets. Translations added for all 13 locales.

Addresses #292 — last resort for devices where all other auto-start
mechanisms fail because the system truly never broadcasts anything.

Add "Start on screen on" to close-on-disconnect warning dialog

The close-on-disconnect modal now warns about the conflict with
"Start on screen on" — enabling both creates a restart loop where
the app closes on disconnect then immediately reopens on screen on.

Start service on boot when "Start on screen on" is enabled

The SCREEN_ON receiver is dynamic (registered in AapService), so the
service must be alive to catch it. On Quick Boot head units that do a
real reboot, the process dies and nobody listens for SCREEN_ON.

Fix: BootCompleteReceiver now also checks autoStartOnScreenOn and
starts the foreground service after boot so the dynamic receiver gets
registered. Added device-protected storage sync for the setting so it
can be read during locked boot.

Also ensure the service starts when the app opens or saves settings
with screen-on auto-start enabled, and fix backgroundTint namespace
for light mode compatibility.

Fix settings crash on Android 4.2 caused by API 21+ layout attributes

The info banner layout used android:backgroundTint and android:tint on
ImageView, both of which require API 21+ and crash on Android 4.2
(API 17) with InflateException.

Replace android:backgroundTint with a dedicated layer-list drawable
that bakes the blue tint into the background, and replace android:tint
with app:tint which is handled by AppCompatImageView on all API levels.

Also switch the exit button's android:backgroundTint to app:backgroundTint
in both fragment_home layouts as a precautionary compat fix.

Handle SecurityException in WifiDirectManager and harden service teardown

init block in try-catch so WiFi Direct gracefully degrades to unavailable
instead of crashing AapService.onCreate.

Also guard unregisterReceiver calls in AapService.onDestroy to prevent
IllegalArgumentException if a receiver was never registered, and use
ContextCompat.registerReceiver in MicRecorder for Android 14+ compat.

Add wake lock and task-removal resilience to resist Quick Boot force-stop

On MediaTek/Reglink head units that reboot with ACC off (Quick Boot),
the firmware force-stops third-party apps ~60-90s after boot to save
power. This kills HUR even though BOOT_COMPLETED was received and the
service started successfully.

Changes:
- Acquire a PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK (10min timeout) when the service starts
  from boot, screen-on, or USB check. This keeps the CPU active and
  signals to the power management system that the service needs to
  stay alive.
- Add stopWithTask="false" to AapService manifest declaration so the
  service survives task removal from recents.
- Add onTaskRemoved() handler that attempts to restart the service.
- Log battery optimization exemption status on boot start.
- Log wake lock state in onDestroy for diagnostics.

Add built-in Quick Boot diagnostic heartbeat logger

When AapService starts from boot or screen-on, writes a heartbeat file
to /sdcard/headunit-quickboot-diag.txt every 2 seconds with timestamp,
uptime, ACC signal status, and wake lock state.

The file persists even after the firmware force-stops the app, so users
can open it from the radio's file manager to see exactly when HUR was
killed — no ADB or PC connection needed.

Header includes system info (boot reason, platform, IPO state, battery
optimization status). Each heartbeat line shows whether the service is
still alive and holding its wake lock.

Add Quick Boot compatibility warning to auto-start settings

Adds an info banner in the auto-start settings screen warning users
that head units with Quick Boot enabled may not support auto-start
features. The Quick Boot shutdown process force-stops third-party apps,
setting them to Android's "stopped" state which blocks all implicit
broadcasts including BOOT_COMPLETED.

The recommended workaround for most users is to disable Quick Boot in
their head unit's system settings.

Translations added for all 13 locales.

Update auto-start warning with DuraSpeed guidance

DuraSpeed (MediaTek's background process manager) was identified as
the actual cause of Quick Boot force-stops on MediaTek head units.
Whitelisting HUR in DuraSpeed solves the auto-start issue without
needing to disable Quick Boot or install as a system app.

Updated the warning banner to guide users to find DuraSpeed in their
system settings. On some head units DuraSpeed is hidden and may
require an app like "Hidden Settings" to access.

Translations updated for all 13 locales.

Add customizable vehicle information settings

Adds a new "Vehicle information" sub-screen in Settings that lets users
customize the identity sent to the phone during the Android Auto
handshake. Previously these values were hardcoded as "Google" and

- Display name (shown on phone, e.g. "Honda Civic")
- Vehicle make, model, and year
- Vehicle ID (with warning that changing it resets AA preferences)
- Driver position (moved from main settings)
- Head unit make and model

The ServiceDiscoveryResponse now reads all values from Settings instead
of using hardcoded strings. Changes take effect on the next AA connection.

Useful for users with multiple vehicles who want to distinguish them
in their phone's Android Auto settings.

because the system WiFi has not yet connected to saved networks. This

Disable USB system modal when auto-start on USB is off

UsbAttachedActivity was registered with a wildcard USB device filter
that matched ALL USB devices, causing Android to show an "Open with
Headunit Revived?" modal for non-Android Auto devices (DACs, mice,
keyboards, etc.) even when USB auto-start was disabled.

Fix: disable UsbAttachedActivity component by default in the manifest
and dynamically enable/disable it via PackageManager when the user
toggles the auto-start on USB setting. The component state is also
synced on app launch to cover first install and app updates.

Fix Japanese locale directory name (values-jp → values-ja)

The ISO 639-1 language code for Japanese is "ja", not "jp" (which is
the country code). This caused Android to not recognize the locale
properly, displaying "Jp" instead of the correct language name in the
language selector.

Optimize UsbAttachedActivity component toggle

Skip redundant setComponentEnabledSetting calls by checking the
current state first, and move the sync call in MainActivity to a
background thread to avoid IPC on the main thread during startup.

- Resolution recommendation based on actual device screen
- Fallback to default overlay if file is missing or corrupt

- Files copied to internal storage (no external permissions needed)

Show custom loading screen during auto-connect

The custom loading screen was previously only visible inside
AapProjectionActivity, which means users saw the home screen briefly
before the projection activity launched on auto-connect, single-USB
auto-connect, self-mode auto-start, and USB auto-attach flows.

Add a mirrored overlay in activity_main.xml that covers the home
screen during automatic connection attempts, driven by a CommManager
connection-state observer:

- Show on Connecting / Connected / StartingTransport when
  beginAutoConnect was requested.
- Hide on HandshakeComplete / TransportStarted (success — projection
  activity covers us with its own overlay using the same media).
- Hide on Error or Disconnected after advancing to an active state
  (failure — drop back to home so the user can intervene).
- 30 s watchdog catches USB open hangs and silent AOA-mode-switch
  failures, neither of which today produces an event for the
  observer to react to.
- Watchdog is restarted on configuration changes so it survives
  activity recreation while the connection attempt continues.
- Overlay is hidden in onStop to free video and animation
  resources when the activity is backgrounded.

Triggered from HomeFragment auto-connect entry points and from
MainActivity itself when launched via UsbAttachedActivity with
EXTRA_LAUNCH_SOURCE = "USB auto-start". Manual button clicks are
intentionally not covered.

Extend auto-connect overlay to manual connection paths

For visual consistency with the auto-connect flow, the loading
overlay now also covers the home screen during connections
initiated by manual user actions:

- HomeFragment: Self Mode button, WiFi mode 1 (Auto/Headunit Server)
  scan, WiFi mode 2 helper scan (non-Nearby), Native AA Bluetooth
  device selector.
- UsbListFragment: device click in accessory mode and the AOA
  mode-switch flow.
- NetworkListFragment: scan-found auto-connect and manual list
  click.

The Nearby device selector is intentionally skipped — its dialog
already has a built-in 'connecting to X' UI showing the device
name, which the overlay would otherwise hide.

Show device-specific status text on Nearby connections

The Nearby device selector previously stayed open with its own
'Connecting to <device>...' UI while the connection completed. With
the auto-connect overlay covering manual paths now, that internal
UI was effectively unreachable.

Hand off the Nearby selection to the auto-connect overlay and pass
the picked device name through as a custom status string. The
overlay displays 'Connecting to Pixel 8...' (or whatever the user
picked) on top of the custom loading media when the show-text
toggle is enabled, preserving the device-name feedback that the
in-dialog UI used to provide.

Adds an optional customStatusText parameter to beginAutoConnect()
that overrides R.string.android_auto_starting on both the default
and custom-media text overlays. Removed three unused locals from
showNearbyDeviceSelector that were only referenced by the removed
in-dialog connecting UI swap.

Carry custom status text into AapProjectionActivity loading screen

The auto-connect overlay in MainActivity already shows context-
specific text such as 'Connecting to Pixel 8…' for the Nearby flow.
Once the handshake completes and AapProjectionActivity takes over
the UI, its own loading screen used to revert to the generic
'Android Auto is starting…' for the 1-2 seconds before the first
video frame arrives.

Add a one-shot pendingStatusText handover slot on the projection
activity. MainActivity writes it whenever beginAutoConnect runs
(including with null to overwrite stale values). The projection
activity reads and clears it at the start of setupCustomLoadingScreen
so the override applies whether or not custom media is configured
and can't leak into a later connection. On the failure path
MainActivity also clears the slot defensively, since AAP will not
launch to consume it.

Address gemini-code-assist review feedback on PR #371

Four fixes from the bot review:

1. (high) Move loading-screen file copy off the main thread.
   LoadingScreenFragment.handleFileSelected was running statSize, the
   previous-media cleanup and a 10 MB copyTo synchronously on the UI
   thread, risking ANR on slow storage (SD card, cloud-backed
   document providers). Wrap the I/O block in
   viewLifecycleOwner.lifecycleScope.launch with Dispatchers.IO and
   bring success/failure outcomes back to main for the toast and
   settings update.

2. (medium) Replace customImage!! with customImage?.let {} in
   AapProjectionActivity. The non-null assertion was technically
   safe given the earlier ?. checks but would crash silently if the
   layout is ever restructured.

3. (medium) Cancel the Ken Burns ObjectAnimator. The infinite-repeat
   scale animator was started but never stored or stopped; it kept
   issuing frame callbacks after the loading overlay was hidden.
   Store it in kenBurnsAnimator and cancel it in
   stopCustomLoadingMedia.

4. (medium) Call stopCustomLoadingMedia from onDestroy. Covers the
   case where the activity is destroyed without going through a
   normal hide path (early connection failure, system kill,
   recreate-before-first-frame), so the VideoView surface and the
   animator are released promptly.

Animate the loading-screen preview for videos and static images

The small preview above 'Tap the preview to see it fullscreen' was
showing a frozen first frame for videos and a still image for
static-image media. The fullscreen preview already handled both
cases correctly; this brings the inline preview to parity.

For videos the preview now plays through a SurfaceView added to
preview_area at runtime, with a MediaPlayer that respects the
loop and aspect-ratio settings — same pattern as
setupFullscreenVideo. The default Glide.load fallback only
extracts a thumbnail, which is what produced the frozen-frame
behaviour.

For static images the preview now applies the same Ken Burns slow
zoom that the live AAP loading screen uses when keep-aspect-ratio
is on, so the user sees the actual animation they're configuring.

Added a clearPreviewMedia helper that releases the MediaPlayer,
removes the dynamically added SurfaceView, and cancels the Ken
Burns animator. It is called from releaseMediaPlayers (so all
existing teardown points — onPause, onDestroyView, file swap,
removeMedia — pick it up automatically) and at the start of every
loadImagePreview call so consecutive reloads (e.g. toggling
aspect ratio) don't stack media on top of each other.

Move loading screen entry to the end of the Graphic group

The loading-screen setting was wedged between Custom Insets and
Start in Fullscreen Mode, which made it easy to miss. Moving it to
the bottom of the Graphic section (after Stretch to Fill / Forced
Scale) surfaces it as a new addition to existing users without
disrupting the order of the long-established entries above it.

Split auto-connect indicator into pill and overlay modes

The full-screen auto-connect loading overlay was blocking the home
screen on every automatic attempt, including launches with no phone
available. Users had to wait up to 30 seconds (the watchdog timeout)
before the home buttons became tappable again. Reported on issue #476.

Introduce ConnectionUiMode with two visual modes:

- PILL: a small, non-blocking status indicator at the top of the home
  screen (reuses the existing wifi_direct_info pill pattern). Used for
  fully automatic background attempts (auto-connect last session,
  single-USB, self-mode auto-start, USB auto-attach). Home buttons stay
  tappable. Tap the pill to cancel the attempt.

- OVERLAY: the existing full-screen custom loading screen with video or
  image. Used for connections the user explicitly initiated by tapping
  a button (Self Mode, WiFi scan, USB list, Native AA, Nearby select).
  A new Cancel button in the top-right dismisses the overlay, and Back
  press is now also wired to cancel.

beginAutoConnect() takes a mode parameter; all 14 call sites updated.
endAutoConnect() now also clears the pill so a mid-attempt mode switch
or recreation cannot leave a stale view visible.

Also fix the AapService ACTION_DISCONNECT handler: it previously
guarded on isConnected, which excludes the Connecting state, so a
DisconnectIntent during a pending attempt was silently dropped. Now it
fires for any non-Disconnected state.

Address PR review feedback

- Move autoConnectStatusText and hasAdvancedToActiveState to the
  companion alongside autoConnectInProgress and autoConnectMode. As
  instance fields they were lost on activity recreation (rotation,
  theme change), which dropped the customized status text from the
  Nearby selector and reset the active-state tracking so a real
  mid-attempt Disconnect could be misread as the initial Disconnected
  on launch.
- Drop the redundant connection-state guard in
  AapService.ACTION_DISCONNECT. CommManager.disconnect() already
  early-returns when the state is Disconnected, and unlike the old
  isConnected check the new guard wasn't actually needed because
  disconnect() also handles the Connecting state internally.

Move auto-connect pill to bottom-center

The pill was anchored to top-center, which overlapped with the
wifi_direct_info status pill that uses the same anchor. Result was
two stacked translucent pills with unreadable text whenever helper
mode was active during an auto-connect attempt.

Move the pill to bottom-center. That spot is empty on the home
screen: the Exit button is in the bottom-right corner and nothing
else is anchored to the bottom edge, so no further conflicts.

Seed hasAdvancedToActiveState and gate pill on real attempts

Two related correctness fixes for the auto-connect pill flow:

1. beginAutoConnect now seeds hasAdvancedToActiveState from the
   current CommManager state. If something outside the activity
   (typically AapService reacting to a USB attach) had already moved
   the state into Connecting before we got here, the StateFlow would
   not re-emit it, so the observer would never flip the flag on its
   own and a subsequent failure transition to Disconnected would be
   misread as the initial Disconnected on launch, leaving the pill
   stuck until the watchdog fires.

2. attemptAutoConnect and attemptSingleUsbAutoConnect now return a
   Boolean indicating whether a connection attempt was actually
   dispatched. The HomeFragment auto-connect call sites only show
   the pill when the attempt method confirms work was queued. Without
   this, the pill could appear for 30 s even when the attempt was a
   no-op (Native AA mode, no last session, missing USB device or
   permission, disclaimer not yet accepted).

Block Native AA wireless flow while another session is active

When AapService starts (e.g. on USB attach), it always brings up Native
AA mode 3 wireless infrastructure (WiFi Direct group, BT handshake
server, A2DP poke). With a USB session already running, the BT poke
still fires and the BT handshake still pushes WiFi credentials, so the
phone gets dragged into a parallel wireless connection attempt that
cannot succeed because it is already projecting over USB.

Gate the auto-poke and the BT handshake response on the current
CommManager state. If a session is already connected or connecting,
skip the poke and abort the handshake instead of telling the phone to
start a new wireless session. Manual pokes (user pressing the WiFi
button) are unchanged.

Persist Auto-Optimize wizard settings synchronously

The Auto-Optimize wizard writes resolution, DPI, view mode, video codec and
screen orientation directly to SharedPreferences via apply(), which is
asynchronous. If the process is killed before the write reaches disk (for
example after the user starts Self Mode and the system reclaims the app),
the changes are lost on the next launch. Call commit() so the write blocks
until it lands on disk, matching how other immediate-apply settings (screen
orientation, fullscreen mode) already persist themselves.

Also refresh the SettingsFragment pending state from SharedPreferences once
the wizard finishes, so the queued recreate() cannot race with a stale Save
that would overwrite the wizard's values with the pre-wizard pending vars.

Fixes andreknieriem/headunit-revived#504

Refresh settings list before recreate after wizard apply

The RecyclerView did not reflect the wizard's new pending state until
the activity finished recreating, which can lag on slower devices and
briefly show stale values.

Cache commManager on NativeAaHandshakeManager

Avoids repeating the App.provide(context).commManager lookup in
triggerPoke() and handleHandshake(), and drops the redundant fully
qualified CommManager reference now that the property lives in the
same package.

Skip permanent audio focus in dynamic mode (issue #654)

Only request permanent AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN in requestPermanentAudioFocus when
Static Audio Focus is enabled. In the default dynamic mode, focus is
acquired on demand, so grabbing permanent gain on connect needlessly
evicts other media (e.g. the car radio) before AA plays anything.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Gate eager audio focus grab in startReading() (issue #654)

CommManager.startReading() unconditionally requested a permanent
AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN on STREAM_MUSIC on every connect, ignoring both the
enableAudioSink and staticAudioFocus settings, which evicted other media
(e.g. the car radio) the moment the phone connected. Gate it behind
enableAudioSink && staticAudioFocus, matching requestPermanentAudioFocus
and AapControlService.audioFocusRequest; in dynamic mode focus is
acquired on demand instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Acquire transient audio focus while AA audio plays (dynamic mode)

In dynamic mode the app only acquired system audio focus in response to
a protocol AudioFocusRequestNotification(GAIN). Some phones never send
GAIN when media starts — the always-grant handshake makes them assume
the head unit permanently holds focus — so the head unit never grabbed
focus and other local sources (e.g. the car radio) kept playing
alongside AA audio.

Track active AA audio channels and hold AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN_TRANSIENT while
any channel is playing, releasing when the last one stops. TRANSIENT
(not permanent GAIN) makes the other source pause during playback and
resume afterwards rather than being permanently stopped. Gated on
!staticAudioFocus && enableAudioSink; composes idempotently with the
protocol-driven focus path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Capture volatile _transport into a local in startReading()

Read the @Volatile _transport once at the top of startReading() and bail
out early if it's null. A concurrent disconnect can clear _transport
between reads, so a stable local reference avoids the race and prevents
emitting TransportStarted when no reading actually started.

Recover automatically from post-first-frame video display stalls

On some head units the display consumer (the GL thread on GLES, or the
TextureView) stops drawing shortly after the first frame while the decoder
keeps producing frames. The picture freezes, often on the Android Auto boot
logo, while audio keeps playing. The only workaround so far was to press
Home and reopen the app, which rebuilds the surface (issue #650).

Add a per-backend "last frame drawn" signal (GL thread draw for GLES,
onSurfaceTextureUpdated for TextureView, unsupported for plain SurfaceView)
and a watchdog that rebuilds the projection view automatically when the
decoder is still producing frames but the display has not drawn for several
seconds. The recovery is narrow (it ignores phone-side pauses, which stall
the decoder too and are handled by the reconnecting overlay) and bounded by
a cooldown and a max attempt count to avoid rebuild loops.

Refine display-stall recovery with input-side signal and SurfaceView fallback

Base the issue #650 recovery on two signals instead of the decoder-release
timestamp, which can keep advancing while nothing reaches the screen. Add
VideoDecoder.lastInputBytesReceivedMs (stamped when encoded bytes arrive from
the phone) and trigger recovery only when the phone is still streaming but the
display consumer has not drawn for several seconds. A phone-side pause stops
the input too and stays with the reconnecting overlay.

When a device keeps stalling after a plain surface rebuild, escalate once to
SurfaceView for the rest of the session (the most direct path, which avoids the
external-texture route that the logs show as the bottleneck on MediaTek). The
override is session-scoped, never persisted, and is skipped while the bundled
software HEVC decoder is active since it renders through the GLES YUV sink.

Bug: AAP transport gets stuck after repeated reconnects because _transport remains in invalid state after quit

When using Android Auto wireless projection, the first disconnect works correctly. After reconnecting and disconnecting again, the application can enter a stuck state.

The issue appears after multiple connect/disconnect cycles. AapTransport.quit() is called, but the next quit attempt shows that onQuit callback is already null, while _transport still references the old AapTransport instance.

Detect low-fps display collapse and reset stall recovery counter

The MediaTek GLES stall is not a clean freeze: the consumer keeps drawing but
drops to 2-5fps with single frames taking up to around 2s, so the previous
"no frame drawn for N seconds" check never fired. Add a per-view long-frame

a sliding window, alongside the existing full-freeze check. Also recover when
the consumer never drew a single frame after the overlay was dismissed, and
reset the recovery counter after a sustained healthy period so the mechanism
is not permanently disabled on a long drive.

Recommend SurfaceView over GLES for older devices with hardware decode

The auto-optimize wizard recommended GLES for all Android 5.0-8.1 devices.
Sampling the hardware decoder's external texture in-app via GLES forces a
per-frame color conversion on some SoCs (MediaTek's MDP), which collapses
playback to a few fps while audio keeps going (issue #650). That is why
affected head units end up on the failing path, and why Home and reopen (a
fresh surface) recovers it.

Recommend a direct SurfaceView for these devices when they can decode video
in hardware, keeping GLES only where the software YUV sink is actually needed.
Also log the recommended and active view mode with the SoC so the path can be
confirmed from device logs.

Update WifiDirectManager.kt

Only treat genuine Nearby sockets as single-message transports

SocketAccessoryConnection.isSingleMessage was hardcoded true for every
transport. It's now only true for NearbySocket; other transports
(WirelessServer-accepted sockets, manual IP) still need the handshake
settle-delay and stale-byte-drain safeguards.

Disable hotspot before starting WiFi Direct

This chipset can't run SoftAP and WiFi Direct concurrently, so
initWifiMode() now disables the hotspot before P2P starts.

Register NSD for the Hotspot helper strategies too

Wireless Helper's discovery on the Hotspot strategies (3, 4) depends
on this service record instead of blindly probing the TCP port, same
as it already does for Common WiFi NSD.

Clear stale lastKnownBssid on every removeGroup() call site

createGroup() assigns a new random GO interface MAC each time, so a
cached BSSID from the torn-down group is stale and must never be
handed to the phone for the new one.

Add reflection-based BSSID fallback for masked P2P MACs

Fallback 6 reflects over WifiP2pGroup/WifiP2pDevice's declared fields
for any unmasked MAC-shaped string, for OEM builds where
NetworkInterface, cached/local/owner addresses, sysfs, and
Settings.Secure all come back masked or permission-denied (reproduced
on a Poco X3/MIUI unit).

Launch projection activity directly on auto-connect success

MainActivity.endAutoConnect(success = true) only hid its own "Connecting..."
overlay, trusting AapProjectionActivity would launch on its own via
AapControl.gainVideoFocus() -> AapBroadcastReceiver's ProjectionActivityRequest
broadcast. That broadcast only fires once the phone's VIDEO
mediaSinkSetupRequest arrives, which can lag several seconds behind
HandshakeComplete. During that gap the overlay was already gone, dropping
the user back on HomeFragment with only a relabeled "To Android Auto"
button as any indication - reproduced live: onCreate for the projection
activity didn't fire until manually tapped, ~6.8s after handshake
completion and after the video mediaSinkSetupRequest had already arrived.

Now calls startActivity() on AapProjectionActivity directly (mirroring the
same pattern already used in onCreate() for bringing an active session back
to front). launchMode="singleTask" means the later gainVideoFocus()
broadcast, once it does arrive, just reuses this same instance instead of
creating a duplicate.

Fix WifiP2pConfig.Builder crash in Native AA 5GHz group creation

Builder.build() requires networkName+passphrase (or a peer address) or
it throws IllegalStateException unconditionally, so every 5GHz group
creation attempt crashed and burned the whole retry budget (~8s) before
falling back to the standard path. Supply a valid autonomous-group name
and passphrase so the 5GHz request succeeds on the first attempt.

Fix WiFi Direct disconnect freeze: key AapRead.Factory off transport shape

810c492 correctly scoped isSingleMessage to genuine Nearby sockets for
the AA 16.4+ handshake settle-delay/drain skip in AapTransport.handshake(),
but AapRead.Factory.create() also keyed its read-loop choice off that same
flag. That flipped WiFi Direct/Hotspot/manual-IP sockets from
AapReadSingleMessage onto AapReadMultipleMessages, which - unlike
AapReadSingleMessage - has never had to recognize the Wireless Helper's
Magic Garbage (16x 0xFF) disconnect signal, since USB/libusb (its only
prior caller) never sees that signal. Result: those bytes get misread as
a header claiming a 65535-byte body that never arrives, so the read loop
idles forever instead of quitting - the freeze when clicking Disconnect
in Wireless Helper over WiFi Direct.

Every socket-backed transport (Nearby, WiFi Direct, Hotspot, manual IP)
has used AapReadSingleMessage successfully for years; only USB/libusb
ever needed AapReadMultipleMessages's FIFO reassembly, because bulk
transfers can batch multiple messages into one read in a way socket
recv() doesn't. So key the Factory choice on transport shape
(connection is SocketAccessoryConnection) instead of isSingleMessage,
restoring that assignment without touching the handshake-timing fix
810c492 made. This avoids duplicating the Magic Garbage detection logic
across two read-loop implementations.

Cap negotiated video resolution to the head unit panel

The app advertised the video resolution to the phone without ever capping it to
the physical panel, so a 1024x600 head unit could receive 1920x1080 and downscale
1080p to 600p every frame. On MediaTek that downscale runs through the MDP scaler
and collapses playback to a few fps while audio keeps going (issue #650); it is
backend independent, which is why switching to SurfaceView did not help.

Cap the negotiated resolution to the native resolution the panel warrants (reusing
the existing AUTO selection against the physical panel size), so it is only ever
lowered, never raised. Also stop the setup wizard from recommending 1080p on small
high-DPI panels (it keyed off densityDpi), and log the resolution decision so the
path can be confirmed from device logs.

Add manual-coordinate night mode and geofenced day/night with automation gating

Adds a Manual Coordinates night mode so head units without GPS can compute
sunrise/sunset from a fixed point picked on a map (issue #647), and extends it
into named geofenced areas. Each area can force day or night while the device is
inside it and can optionally restrict auto-start/auto-connect to that area.

Live location comes from the head unit GPS or the phone-forwarded GPS during
projection. The automation gate fails open when no location is available so
devices without GPS are never blocked. The picker uses an OpenStreetMap (Leaflet)
map in a WebView shown after an internet-required notice.

Night mode list and new strings updated across all locales.

Reworks the round 1 UX so it is clearer and covers the app theme too.

Manual coordinates are no longer a separate night mode. Instead the Auto
(sunrise/sunset) modes gain a location source (GPS or a fixed point picked on the
map), and that fixed point is shared by both the app theme and the Android Auto
night mode, so head units without GPS get correct day/night in both.

Saved places now have two independent capabilities: forcing a theme (with a scope
of App, Android Auto, or both) and gating auto-start/connect. A place that does
neither cannot be saved. While inside a place that forces a theme it wins over the
selected mode, shown with a note and a live status line.

source only appears for Auto modes, "pick on map" only when the fixed point is
chosen, and the scope and dark/light controls only when the place forces a theme.

Simplify location UX and fix geofence activation

Fixes two reasons a place would not take effect when inside it. Geofence checks no
longer discard the location just because the last GPS fix is old, which is normal
in a parked car, so the last known position is used regardless of age. The app
theme engine now also runs when a saved place can force the app theme, so the
override applies even when the app theme is a fixed mode.

Reworks the screen so it is easier to follow. All location settings now live in one
self-contained Location screen (the sunrise/sunset reference point and the saved
places), and the theme selectors no longer carry inline location controls or notes.
In the place editor the two theme switches are replaced by a single Off / Light /
Dark choice, and the scope only appears when an appearance is chosen. Manual
coordinates are set through the sunrise reference, not a separate night mode.

Make Location a theme mode; drop scope, automation gate and notes

"Location (by area)" option. Its sub-options (the outside-places appearance and
the saved places) only appear when it is selected, so nothing clutters the other

Fix recreate loop when opening the places screen

Opening the places screen made the app flicker and become unusable. Its onResume
re-applied the app theme on every resume, and re-applying builds a fresh theme
engine that always signals a theme change, which recreates the activity, which
resumes the fragment again, looping forever.

The places screen no longer re-applies on resume. Saving or deleting a place now
re-evaluates the existing theme engine instead of rebuilding it, so a recreate
only happens when the appearance actually changes, never in a loop.

Move Location options into their own group with an Applies to selector

When either the app theme or the Android Auto night mode is set to Location, the
location options no longer hang off the theme sections. They now live in a
dedicated Location group that appears whenever either selector uses Location.

The group has an Applies to selector (App, Android Auto, Both) that reflects and
drives which selectors use Location. Choosing there updates the two selectors above

Center the fixed point picker on the device with an accuracy circle; raise radius to 5 km

Picking the fixed sunrise/sunset point on the map now opens centered on the

Also raises the maximum place radius from 2000 to 5000 meters.

Resize content for the soft keyboard so text fields are not covered

The name field in the map picker was hidden behind the keyboard because the
window did not make room for it. The shared system UI handler consumed all window
insets and padded only for the system bars, ignoring the keyboard inset, so the
content never shrank when the keyboard opened.

It now also pads for the IME inset, so any screen's content shrinks while the
keyboard is up (zero when it is hidden). The settings activity is marked
adjustResize for older devices, and the map can shrink so the name field stays
visible above the keyboard.

Show the live place status as info text and add a configurable radius to the point picker

The "currently inside" status on the places screen looked like a tappable option.
It is now shown as live info text (the info banner supports a dynamic string), so
it reads as a status, not a setting.

The fixed sunrise/sunset point picker now shows the configurable radius slider and
circle like the place editor, instead of a static accuracy circle that did not
appear without a GPS fix. The radius defaults to the saved value, then the GPS
accuracy, then a sensible default, and is remembered.

Make manual coordinate entry locale-proof and show the supported format

The coordinate dialog prefilled and parsed numbers with the device locale, so on
locales that use a comma decimal separator the prefilled value and comma input were
rejected as invalid. It now prefills with a dot and accepts either a dot or a comma
when parsing, and shows labels and a short help line with the supported format and
an example.

Settings redesign and onboarding wizard

Deliver credentials when reusing an existing WiFi Direct group

When an existing P2P group was found, the reuse path only logged and returned, so
onGroupInfoAvailable never ran and the group credentials (SSID, passphrase, IP and
BSSID) were never delivered to the phone. The phone could not auto-join the reused
group, so it had to be connected by hand through the Wireless Helper and the silent
auto-reconnect was lost.

Now the reuse path resolves the device info and requests the group info the same way
the freshly created group path does, so the credentials are delivered and the phone
can auto-join again.

Restore the WiFi Launcher wake so the helper auto-launches again (#719)

In WiFi Helper mode the head unit wakes the phone's Wireless Helper by opening a
TCP probe to port 5289 and holding it open briefly, so the helper detects the
inbound socket and launches itself. When the two NetworkDiscovery files were
consolidated, the 500ms hold was dropped and the probe socket is now closed
instantly, so the helper is no longer woken when it is not already running and
the user has to open it by hand.

Hold the 5289 probe open ~500ms again before closing, and add diagnostic logging
around the wake (probe held, probe released, and a failed-probe line) so a
connection log clearly shows whether the helper wake fired. This is the WiFi
Launcher / phone-hotspot path, separate from the WiFi Direct group fix in #722.

Add a permissions step to the setup wizard

Fresh installs used to be hit with a burst of permission prompts right after
the wizard, because MainActivity requested them blindly on launch while the
wizard opened on top, and per-feature prompts fired later on the home screen.

The wizard now shows an explained permissions checklist just before the final
summary: each entry has a help line describing what it is for, a green check
when already granted, an Allow button otherwise, and an Enable all button that
requests the normal permissions in a single dialog. Special access (display over
other apps, modify system settings) opens its own screen per row.

Permissions come from a central AppPermissions registry, so adding a future
permission is a single entry plus its two strings, with no wizard or layout
changes. The same list is reachable from Settings > Permissions (PermissionsFragment)
for users who already finished onboarding, and MainActivity now only requests
permissions directly when the wizard will not run. Strings translated to all
ten locales.

Preserve the user DPI in the wizard and suggest the loading screen

Re-running the setup wizard used to overwrite a user-chosen DPI: the DPI picker
was always seeded with the recommended value and applied on Next, so a value set
by hand in Settings was silently replaced. The picker now seeds from the saved
DPI when the user already set one, and the recommended value is shown as a hint
below the picker instead of being forced. Fresh installs still start at the
recommendation, since there is no saved value to keep.

The final wizard step now also invites the user to set a custom loading screen,
with a button that finishes onboarding and opens the loading screen setup
directly. Strings translated to all ten locales.
Center the loading screen suggestion on the wizard final step

Guard the auto-hotspot behind WRITE_SETTINGS with a clear message

Enabling the head unit's own hotspot uses reflective startTethering / setWifiApEnabled,
which the framework gates behind the special WRITE_SETTINGS access. Without it the app
threw a SecurityException and logged a stack trace before giving up. Check
Settings.System.canWrite() first and, when it is missing, log a clear line pointing to
the setup wizard permissions step / Settings > Permissions instead. Also log the
canWriteSettings state up front so a connection log shows the permission status.

Keep the sunrise Auto mode selected when opening the map (#647)

When the app theme or Android Auto night mode was set to Auto (sunrise/sunset)
but not yet saved, opening the coordinate picker or the map deselected the mode.
Navigating to the map recreated the fragment, which re-read the still-unsaved
mode from settings and reverted the selection, so the user had to save the mode
first before saving a map point.

The fixed-point flow now commits the pending Auto mode and the fixed source to
settings before entering coordinates or opening the map, and asks the service to
re-send the Android Auto night mode. On return the picked point is reflected in
the coordinate fields. The app theme is only refreshed when not navigating away,
to avoid an activity recreate in the middle of the navigation.

Add timeout to Native AA handshake response wait

readProtobuf() called input.readFully() with no timeout after sending
WifiStartRequest, so a phone that never replies left the handshake
blocked forever with no error and no retry. BluetoothSocket has no
setSoTimeout(), so a watchdog now force-closes the socket after 15s to
unblock the read and surface a clear failure instead of hanging.

Re-arm Native AA handshake manager on Bluetooth reconnect

AutoStartReceiver started AapService with a bare intent (no action) on a
trusted-device ACL_CONNECTED event. If the service process was already
alive from an earlier session in the same process lifetime, onCreate()'s
initWifiMode() never re-runs, and the null-action fallback in
onStartCommand did nothing — so a Native AA handshake manager that had
been stopped (e.g. after a user exit) stayed dead forever despite the
phone reconnecting over Bluetooth. Gearhead's RFCOMM connect then fails
instantly since nothing is listening on the AA SDP UUID.

AutoStartReceiver now sends an explicit ACTION_BT_AUTO_START, handled by
re-arming wireless mode only when the handshake manager isn't already
active, avoiding a redundant group teardown/recreate right behind a
fresh onCreate.

Also fixes a related latent bug in NativeAaHandshakeManager.start():
isRunning was set true before checking whether the Bluetooth adapter was
ready, so a single early call during adapter init (e.g. at boot) could
leave isRunning stuck true with no listener ever actually opened,
permanently defeating both this new re-arm check and manual pokes
(matches the symptom in #706 — no "Connection accepted" or "ACTIVELY
LISTENING" log ever appears despite a successful poke).

Experimental: listen for Native AA on secondary Bluetooth radios (#706)

Some head units have two Bluetooth radios (for example K706 and CAR8032). Native AA
opened its RFCOMM listener only on the default radio, so a phone bonded to the other
one never reached it and Android Auto reported the phone as not detected. This also
opens the AA and HFP listeners on any other radio that reports a real, different
address. It is a strict no-op on the usual single-radio device, and it is skipped when
the address is masked (API 31+), so it cannot disturb the primary listener. Complements
the handshake reliability fix in #725 (different code path: adapter selection).

Experimental: recreate a stale WiFi Direct group instead of reusing it (#719 #703)

A persistent P2P group survives reboots. When a group existed that we did not create
this session, the code reused it and advertised its credentials, so the phone re-prompted
to accept a group it no longer trusts (the repeated accept prompts, and works-once-then-
fails-after-reboot). Track whether the group was created this session; if a pre-existing
group is stale, remove it and create a fresh one, the way it behaved before groups were
reused. The confirmed intra-session reuse path is preserved unchanged.

Fix WiFi Direct group reuse regression and restore pre-join discovery loop

checkGroupAndCreate() now unconditionally tears down and recreates the P2P
group on every reuse (via deletePersistentGroup() reflection, not just
removeGroup(), since the latter alone leaves the group's persistent profile
intact and the recreated group comes back with the same networkId/SSID).
ebab63a8 turned this into a no-op for reused groups, which lets a peer's
WPS/PBC registrar expectations desync from the client and spin into a tight
internal PROV-DISC retry loop; confirmed via live-device bisection that
reverting only that commit's change restores reliability. A checkGroupAndCreateInFlight
reentrancy guard replaces an earlier 3s wall-clock debounce that was gating
the teardown - live testing showed reuse itself, not teardown frequency,
causes the retry storm, and the guard already prevents the concurrent-call
pattern that caused ebab63a8's original BUSY-chip reports.

Also restores the periodic P2P discovery loop (discoveryRunnable /
isClientConnected) that PR #693 removed. That removal fixed a real bug
(periodic discovery disrupting an already-connected client) that had
already been fixed elsewhere by 1797bb41, so PR #693's removal traded away
real value: live A/B testing with checkGroupAndCreate() held identical
showed the loop measurably improves whether a fresh join completes at all
(4/4 vs 0/2 clean failures). Restored gated on isClientConnected instead of
isConnected so it still stops once a real client joins and only restarts if
that client disconnects, preserving the original disruption fix.

Polish WiFi Direct reuse teardown: reset BSSID, trim comments, guard discovery loop

checkGroupAndCreate()'s reuse-teardown path now clears lastKnownBssid before
removeGroup(), matching the convention every other removeGroup() call site
in this file already follows (cfe92cbc) - the recreated group gets a new
random GO interface MAC, so the old BSSID must not be handed to the phone.

Also trims the comment blocks added for the reuse-teardown/discovery-loop
work down to their load-bearing points, dropping the narrated history of
prior failed attempts.

discoveryRunnable now skips its startDiscovery() call (but still reschedules
its next tick) while checkGroupAndCreateInFlight is true, so it doesn't fire
discoverPeers() while the group is mid-teardown/recreate from the reuse path
or the stuck-retry self-heal.

Give the Native AA quiet-host path the WiFi Direct group protections from #730 (#706)

Native mode (wifiConnectionMode 3) creates its own WiFi Direct group via
startNativeAaQuietHost(), a separate path from the Helper mode checkGroupAndCreate()
that #730 fixed. The native path only did removeGroup() before creating, never
deletePersistentGroup(), and had no re-advertise or self-heal loop, so a stale persistent
group left over from a previous session or reboot desynced the phone's WPS/PBC registrar
into an endless 'Android is connecting...' loop with nothing to recover it.

This brings the native path in line with #730 and adds native-specific recovery:
- Purge the persistent group profile (deletePersistentGroup), not just removeGroup, before
  creating a fresh native group, so the recreated group does not come back with the same
  netId/SSID.
- Make the stuck PROV-DISC retry-burst self-heal apply to native mode too (it was gated to
  Helper mode only); it now recreates the native group with a full purge.
- Add a bounded join watchdog: if no phone joins the quiet host within 30s, tear down and
  recreate a fresh group; after a couple of tries drop the forced 5GHz band, for phones that
  cannot join a 5GHz group owner (a second, independent cause of a permanent connecting loop).
- Cancel the watchdog and reset state on client join, disconnect, P2P off, and stop.

The Helper path and o-jcardenass's #730 logic are left unchanged. I cannot test the wireless
paths myself (I use a wireless USB adapter, not WiFi), so this is code-derived; a test build
and a request to confirm are on #706.

Add an extras card to the wizard's last step with keymap and mic shortcuts

The Ready step now shows a card with quick shortcuts to the loading
screen, keymap and microphone settings, so people can jump straight to
the configs the wizard does not cover without hunting for them later.
Each row opens the matching settings screen and finishes the wizard.

Add screen orientation and screen mode to in-projection Quick Settings

These two apply live without a reconnect, so they fit the Quick Settings
overlay meant for fixing something on the fly. Orientation covers the
common case of Android Auto coming up sideways, and screen mode fixes a
status or nav bar covering the projection. Orientation reuses the existing
ACTION_ORIENTATION_CHANGED path; screen mode reapplies via a new flag on
the settings-changed broadcast.

Fix native join watchdog racing the Bluetooth handshake, drop dead persistent-group purge

The native quiet-host join watchdog armed its 30s timer at P2P group-formation
time with no visibility into NativeAaHandshakeManager's Bluetooth handshake,
so it could (and on-device, reliably did) tear the group down and hand out a
new SSID/passphrase while a real handshake was mid-exchange, reproducing the
exact "Android is connecting..." loop it was meant to fix. WifiDirectManager
now checks whether a handshake is in flight before recovering and defers
instead, the timeout is raised to 60s (a healthy BT reconnect was observed
taking ~35s), and NativeAaHandshakeManager's cached credentials are
invalidated right before a recreate as defense in depth. Confirmed on-device:
the watchdog now logs "deferring recovery" instead of recreating mid-handshake.

Also drops the deletePersistentGroup() purge from both the native and
Helper-mode (#730) reuse paths: confirmed on-device that call is rejected
outright for every netId, including the persisted profile's own real one, so
it was never actually purging anything. Both paths fall back to the
removeGroup()+createGroup() teardown, which is the part that actually works.

range, so people see how the size setting changes how much fits on screen
before touching anything. Only the illustration moves: the slider and the
DPI number stay at the real value. The moment the user changes the DPI
(slider, tabs or the value field) the demo stops for good. Applied both in
the setup wizard and the standalone DPI screen, and it never changes the
saved value.

Hide the GPS source choice in Self Mode

Self Mode runs Android Auto on this same device, so there is no separate
phone and the 'this device vs connected phone' GPS choice makes no sense.
The wizard now skips the Location step entirely for Self Mode users (the
step dots follow the visible steps), and the Settings toggle is hidden the
same way. Other setups are unchanged.

Reset handshakeInFlight before the idle Bluetooth session-maintain loop

handshakeInFlight was only reset in handleHandshake()'s finally block,
which doesn't run until the whole function returns — including the
"Maintaining Bluetooth session" loop that runs indefinitely after the
credential exchange is done, until the socket disconnects. That kept the
flag stuck true for the entire lifetime of a completed connection, which
permanently blocked the native join watchdog from ever recovering again
once one handshake had gone through: confirmed on-device after leaving
HUR open for ~35 minutes, the watchdog logged "deferring recovery" every
60s indefinitely with no phone ever joining.

Move the reset to right after the exchange completes, before the maintain
loop. Verified on-device: forced a P2P client drop while keeping Bluetooth
connected, and the watchdog now correctly fires and recreates the group
instead of deferring forever.

Log the local Bluetooth radio on native handshakes

Dual-Bluetooth-radio head units make it hard to tell which radio a phone
actually reached. The accept and handshake logs now print the local radio
address, so a native log can be matched against the head unit MAC the phone
connected to in its own log.

Release Bluetooth connection shortly after WiFi handoff instead of holding it forever

NativeAaHandshakeManager held the AA_UUID Bluetooth socket open
indefinitely after completing the credential handoff (added reactively
in commit 5e48ffb4 as a fix for an unspecified "connection lost" report,
replacing an earlier bounded 20s hold). This kept Bluetooth occupied for
the entire session even though nothing further used that socket.

A reference open-source Android Auto wireless dongle implementation
(nisargjhaveri/WirelessAndroidAutoDongle) hit the identical complaint —
holding Bluetooth open after the handoff caused "confusion, especially
with phone calls" — and confirmed via the real Android-side protocol
behavior that Bluetooth is expected to close right after the WiFi
credential exchange completes (issues/17, fixed in PR #18).

Now closes the socket ~3s after sending the WifiInfoResponse instead of
holding it indefinitely. Verified on-device: WiFi handoff, full AA
session (AapService.onConnected, GEARHEAD_PROJECTION_MODE_STARTED), and
2+ minutes of stable operation all completed normally after the
Bluetooth socket was already released — no regression of the original
"connection lost" symptom this replaces.

Stop accepting AA_UUID connections after handoff, not just closing the socket

Closing just the client socket after a successful handoff (previous
commit) wasn't enough: the phone reads that as an unexpected drop and
immediately retries connecting to the still-listening AA_UUID server,
which accepts it, bails out in handleHandshake() (already connected),
and closes it again — a tight reconnect storm with no backoff on either
side. Confirmed on-device: hundreds of accept/close cycles a second for
25+ seconds straight, easily mistaken for a Bluetooth pairing loop.

Now closes the AA_UUID server socket(s) too — primary and any secondary
radios — once a handshake hands off successfully, so there's nothing left
for the phone to retry against. HFP listeners are left running. Re-opened
the next time start() runs, which AapService's existing disconnect
handling already does. Verified on-device: single connect/close pair, no
storm, stable session afterward.

Fix isActive() to account for AA listener closing after handoff

Found while auditing the handshake manager's history for regressions
before pushing the recent Bluetooth-release changes. Commit 52fe1087
("Re-arm Native AA handshake manager on Bluetooth reconnect") documents
an invariant AutoStartReceiver's ACTION_BT_AUTO_START handler relies on:
isActive() must mean "genuinely able to accept a connection," not just
"isRunning," specifically so a phone reconnecting over Bluetooth can
re-arm a dead handshake manager instead of silently failing forever.

closeAaListeners() (this branch) closes the AA_UUID listener after a
successful handoff while leaving isRunning true (HFP stays up), which
broke that invariant: isActive() would report true even with nothing
listening on the AA UUID. Confirmed safe to fix directly — AutoStartReceiver
already returns early whenever a WiFi AA session is actively connected, so
tightening isActive() can only ever affect the case where there's already
no live session to protect. Verified on-device: normal handoff still
completes cleanly (single connect/close, no storm) with the fix in place.

Expose a way to await CommManager's async disconnect teardown

disconnect() flips connectionState to Disconnected synchronously, then
launches the actual teardown (ByeByeRequest send + socket close) as a
separate coroutine. Callers that need to know the physical connection
is actually closed, not just that the state changed, had no way to

next commit) needs the identical check - extracted as a pure function
so the two can't drift out of sync, following the ActivityLaunchPolicy
precedent for logic that should be unit-testable without an Android
runtime.

Fix Stop Connection leaving the phone attached to WiFi Direct

"Stop Connection" (in the in-session exit dialog) correctly sends a
ByeByeRequest and closes the transport socket, but never tore down
the WiFi Direct P2P group HUR hosts - the existing "Native AA user
exit" branch even had a comment claiming it did, but only ever called
nativeAaHandshakeManager?.stop() (Bluetooth handshake sockets), never
wifiDirectManager?.stop() (the only place that calls
WifiP2pManager.removeGroup()). The plain WiFi-Direct-Helper case
(mode==2, strategy==1) had no handling here at all.

Net effect: the phone stayed connected to the WiFi Direct network at
the OS level after "Stop Connection", and Wireless Helper - which has
no visibility into WifiP2pManager state, only into whether its own
TCP bridge to HUR is still alive - had no way to learn the session had
ended.

Tear the group down on any user-initiated disconnect while a
WiFi-Direct-hosting mode is active, for both Native AA and the Helper
WiFi-Direct strategy. Deliberately skipped on unexpected disconnects,
which want to keep/reuse the existing group for fast reconnection
(mode==3's re-init and scheduleReconnectIfNeeded() both already rely
on this). Awaits CommManager's async teardown first via
awaitDisconnectComplete(), so the P2P interface is never removed while
the ByeByeRequest/socket-close from disconnect() is still in flight.

Verified on-device (Native AA mode): "Stop Connection" now logs
CommManager teardown completing, then WifiDirectManager.stop() running
and removing the group, and dumpsys wifip2p confirms the group is
actually gone afterward (mGroup null, groupFormed: false) - not just
that the AA session ended.

Repair corrupted protobuf descriptors left by the rename commit

5 of 8 generated proto Java files (Control, Input, Media, NavigationStatus,
Sensors) had their embedded serialized FileDescriptorProto byte strings
edited in-place by the original rename commit - it replaced
"headunitrevived" with "openheadunit" directly inside the length-prefixed
descriptor bytes, desyncing the length prefixes and corrupting the
descriptor. This is exactly the risk flagged when this was first found
(and deliberately left alone at the time), except it turns out the
original rename commit had already made the edit inconsistently: some
files' descriptor bytes were touched (and broken), others weren't.

Confirmed via a real crash: Self Mode on Android Auto 17.4 connects, then
crashes and drops back to the home screen a couple seconds in -
`java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Failed to parse protocol buffer
descriptor for generated code` / `InvalidProtocolBufferException: Protocol
message contained an invalid tag (zero)` at Media.<clinit>, triggered the
first time a real AA session touches a message type from one of the
affected files (e.g. MediaSinkSetupRequest).

Fixed properly instead of hand-patching bytes: parsed each file's original,
uncorrupted descriptor (from the pre-rename source), edited the package
name at the message level via protobuf's own text_format round-trip (not
text substitution on the wire bytes), re-serialized, and regenerated the
descriptorData Java string literal from the corrected bytes. Verified via
round-trip decode-of-own-output before writing, and confirmed end-to-end
on-device: Self Mode on AA 17.4 now connects and holds a full session
(video rendering, no crash) instead of crashing within seconds.
